editorial:
Imagine trying to show the world a beauty that only you can see, but everyone around you thinks you are just losing your mind. That is exactly what you get with this story about Vincent van Gogh. You will see a man who is deeply passionate about his art but constantly fights with his own brain. He has a wonderful relationship with his brother Theo, who stays by his side even when things get messy. When Vincent moves to France to find a fresh start, he meets Paul Gauguin, another painter who is just as loud and stubborn as he is. The vibe is very emotional and colorful, making you feel the stress and the joy of creating something new.

Kir Kirkaldy does a great job bringing the pain and passion of the artist to life. The colors on screen are stunning and look like paintings come to life. While the pacing is a bit slow at times, the acting keeps you interested in how the friendship between the two painters falls apart. You should definitely watch this if you like stories about misunderstood geniuses.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a sad note as Vincent's mental health gets worse. After his fight with Gauguin, he can no longer handle the noise in his head. You see him struggle with his loneliness and the feeling that he failed in life. Eventually, he takes his own life with a gunshot. He dies in the arms of his brother Theo, leaving behind a world of art that people finally start to love after he is gone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about art and real life struggles.
